care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 16 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 16 and in the 20-week extension period
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to understand a bit about your situation.

**First, let me ask about your child:**

How old is your child (or children, if you're claiming for more than one)? 

The age categories that matter are:
- **Under 16** years old
- **16 to 19** years old  
- **20 or over**

Please tell me:
1. How many children you want to claim for
2. Each child's name and age

This will help me guide you through the right eligibility pathway.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 16 years old and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! You have one child - Alex, who is 16 years old.

Since Alex is 16, he falls into the 16-19 age category. For children in this age group, eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether they're in approved education or training.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to know about Alex's current situation regarding education or training:

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In approved education or training** (at school, college, or an approved training program)?
2. **Recently left education** (within the last 20 weeks)?
3. **Neither** - not in education/training and didn't recently leave?

Which of these applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex recently left education - it's been a few months now. He finished his GCSEs and is trying to figure out what to do next.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Since Alex recently left education a few months ago, I need to check if he's still within the extension period where you might still be eligible for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see that there's a **20-week extension period** available for young people aged 16-17 who have recently left education, but there are specific conditions.

Let me ask you some important questions about Alex's situation:

1. **When exactly did Alex finish his education?** (I need to know the specific date or at least which month, so we can check if it's been less than 20 weeks)

2. **Has Alex registered with any of these services:**
   - A government careers service
   - Connexions (careers service)
   - The armed services

The extension is only available if Alex left approved education within the last 20 weeks **AND** has registered with one of these qualifying services. Also, the extension ends either at 20 weeks or when the child turns 18, whichever comes first.

Could you provide these details?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex finished his GCSEs back in June, so it's been about 4 months now. And yes, he did register with the local careers service - we went together to help him figure out what he wants to do next, whether that's college, an apprenticeship, or something else.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me calculate the timeframe:

If Alex finished in June and it's now been about 4 months (so we're around October), that would be approximately **16-17 weeks** since he left education. This means Alex is **still within the 20-week extension period**.

And importantly, Alex **has registered with the local careers service**, which is one of the qualifying services for the extension.

This is good news so far! Since both conditions are met (within 20 weeks AND registered with a qualifying service), we can continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex currently working less than 24 hours per week** (or not working at all)?

For children aged 16 and over, if they're working 24 or more hours per week, they're not eligible for Child Benefit unless they're also in approved education or training.

What's Alex's current work situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at all right now. He's just been at home trying to decide what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex isn't working at all, that meets the requirement (working less than 24 hours per week).

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check about benefits:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right**, such as:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

If Alex is receiving these types of benefits in his own name, it would affect eligibility for Child Benefit. Is Alex receiving any of these benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't receiving any benefits in his own name. He's just been staying at home with me while he figures things out.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is not receiving any benefits in his own right, so we can continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex currently enrolled in any type of apprenticeship?**

This is important because different types of apprenticeships have different rules:
- **English apprenticeships** (all types) - would disqualify
- **Scottish Modern Apprenticeships** - would disqualify  
- **Welsh Foundation Apprenticeships** - are approved (wouldn't disqualify)
- **Other Welsh apprenticeships** - would disqualify

Is Alex in an apprenticeship, and if so, what type and where?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't doing an apprenticeship. Like I said, he's still trying to figure out what he wants to do - whether it's college, an apprenticeship, or getting a job. That's why he registered with the careers service, to get some help deciding.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship, so that's fine.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency status. This is about where **you** (the claimant) live and your residency status in the UK.

**Do any of these apply to you?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common situation)

2. **You have settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme

3. **You have pre-settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme AND:
   - You're working and earning above the National Insurance threshold, OR
   - You're actively looking for work (up to 91 days), OR
   - You have sufficient resources to support yourself and your family financially, OR
   - You're studying with sufficient resources, OR
   - You're a family member of an EEA or Swiss national with the right to reside

4. **You're a Crown servant** living abroad or in certain qualifying countries

Which of these applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. I live in Manchester with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You normally live in the UK, which meets the residency requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to confirm that you are responsible for Alex. Since you mentioned you live in Manchester with Alex, this should be straightforward.

**Are you responsible for Alex in any of these ways?**

1. **You live with Alex** (which you've already mentioned you do)

2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** by paying at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards their care (food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc.)

3. **You pay maintenance** under a court order or agreement

Based on what you've told me, it sounds like you live with Alex. Can you confirm that Alex lives with you in your home in Manchester?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, which clearly establishes that you're responsible for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about other claimants:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member
- Anyone else

Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at a time. If someone else is claiming but you've agreed that you should claim instead, that can be transferred. If there's a dispute about who should claim, HMRC would need to decide.

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me - I'm his main carer and he lives with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's living situation. You've mentioned he lives at home with you, but I need to confirm he's not in any special circumstances:

**Which of these describes Alex's current living situation?**

1. **In hospital** - staying in hospital for an extended period
2. **In care** - placed in local authority care
3. **Fostered** - in a foster care arrangement
4. **Living normally at home** - living with you as normal (which seems to be the case)

Based on what you've told me, it sounds like Alex is living normally at home with you. Can you confirm this is correct and that he's not in hospital, care, or a foster arrangement?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - Alex is living normally at home with me. He's not in hospital, care, or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally at home with you.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! Just one final question:

**Is the local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

For example, are they contributing towards:
- Housing costs
- His living expenses
- His care or maintenance

Generally, you cannot get Child Benefit if the local council is paying for the child. Is the council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance in any way?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. I'm supporting him myself at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Based on all the information you've provided, let me confirm the outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit for Alex!

**Summary of Your Eligibility:**

You meet all the requirements for claiming Child Benefit for your 16-year-old son Alex under the **20-week extension period** for young people who have recently left education.

**Why you're eligible:**

✅ **Alex qualifies** because:
- He's 16 years old (within the 16-19 age range)
- He left education in June (approximately 16-17 weeks ago - still within the 20-week extension period)
- He registered with the local careers service (a qualifying service)
- He's not working 24+ hours per week
- He's not receiving benefits in his own right
- He's not in a disqualifying apprenticeship

✅ **You qualify as a claimant** because:
- You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
- You live with Alex and are responsible for him
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance

---

**⏰ Important Time Limit:**

The 20-week extension will end approximately **4 weeks from now** (around 20 weeks from when Alex left education in June). If Alex hasn't started approved education or training by then, your Child Benefit will stop. However, if he enrolls in approved education or training (like college, A-levels, etc.) before the extension ends, you can continue claiming as long as he remains in approved education.

---

**Next Steps to Claim:**

1. **Apply as soon as possible** - either:
   - **Online** at gov.uk, or
   - **By post** using form CH2

2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex

3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate

4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge:**
   - If you or your partner earns over £60,000, you may need to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through your tax return
   - This doesn't affect your eligibility - you can still claim

5. **Payments:** Child Benefit is usually paid every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

---

**More Information:**
- How to claim: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim
- General eligibility: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

If Alex decides to go to college or start approved education/training, make sure to update HMRC so your Child Benefit can continue beyond the 20-week extension period. Good luck to Alex with his future plans!
